# Sleep

## The problem
The 2-2-4 rotation on 7B at St. Aldric's wrecks me. Two 12-hour days, two 12-hour nights, four off. After the second night I'm basically a zombie until Thursday, and that is exactly when the long run plan wants me fresh. Garmin sleep score average for August 2025 was 61. Sixty-one! I tell patients about sleep hygiene all day and then go home and scroll Reddit at 10 am with the sun blasting in.

Marguerite (club coach, High Park Harriers) said it straight on 2025-08-19: "Protect the sleep before you protect the mileage." Fair.

## What I track
Every morning in the notes app, then copied into the training sheet on Sundays:

- bedtime and wake time (from the Forerunner 265, not my guess)
- Garmin sleep score and overnight HRV average
- resting HR: normal for me is 52, after nights it creeps up to 58 to 60
- coffee after 2 pm yes/no (the actual rules live in [[Caffeine cutoff]])
- training load the day before
- alcohol, even one glass

The resting HR number is the most honest one. If it's 57+ I swap intervals for an easy 6 km.

## Blackout setup (September 2025)
- Hemsley blackout cellular blinds from Home Depot, $139 for the two bedroom windows, installed 2025-09-03
- Manta contoured eye mask, $35, worth every cent
- room thermostat down to 18°C at bedtime, Dev grumbles but sleeps better too
- Dev's old Dohm white noise machine on the low setting, it drowns the streetcar on Roncesvalles
- phone charges in the hallway, I bought a $12 alarm clock from Canadian Tire

## After night shifts
Home around 8:10 am. Small breakfast (toast, yogurt, half a banana), shower, no screens. In bed by 9.

Between the two nights: sleep 9:15 am to about 2:30 pm, up, eat, then a 90 minute nap from 5:30 pm before the second shift. That nap is the whole game.

After the last night: only a short 3 hour block (9 am to noon), then I make myself go outside and walk to the market, so I can fall asleep at 10:30 pm like a normal human. Melatonin 0.5 mg at 9:30 pm on that recovery night only. NOT 5 mg. The 5 mg tablets from Shoppers gave me vivid weird dreams and a groggy morning, and the 0.5 mg works just as well for me.

## When my head won't switch off
Some nights the brain replays the whole shift: the patient in bed 14, the call bell, the charting I forgot.

1. 4-7-8 breathing, five rounds
2. cognitive shuffle: picture random unrelated objects (bucket, lantern, giraffe, envelope...) until it gets boring
3. if nothing after about 20 minutes, get up, sit in the kitchen with the dim lamp and read a paper book. Currently Piranesi, which is perfect because it's calm and odd
4. back to bed only when sleepy, not just tired

Things that did not help: magnesium glycinate 200 mg (no change over 3 weeks, July 2025), the Calm app subscription ($89.99 a year, cancelled).

## Running and sleep
Clear pattern from the summer: the weeks I averaged under 6 hours, my Saturday long run heart rate drifted about 8 bpm higher at the same 6:30/km pace. On 2025-08-16 the 26 km felt like a 32. Also more migraines on short-sleep weeks, see [[Migraine triggers]].

During the taper the goal is 8 hours a night, no exceptions, see [[Marathon taper]]. I already asked Joyce in scheduling to keep me off nights from Oct 12 to race day, and she said yes (she runs too).

## Travel
For the Lisbon trip next spring the plan is in [[Jet lag strategy]]. Short version: shift bedtime by 30 minutes a day for four days before flying.
